title: prefers-reduced-motion and user preferences
learningObjectives: Explain prefers-reduced-motion and user preferences and apply it in an accessible responsive interface.

understand.concept: The prefers-reduced-motion media feature detects whether the user has requested reduced motion at the operating-system or browser level. Other preference features include prefers-color-scheme and forced-colors. CSS can adapt animation, colour scheme, and presentation to these preferences.
understand.whyItMatters: Motion can cause discomfort for some users. Respect reduced-motion preferences by removing or simplifying non-essential movement while preserving meaning and feedback. Do not use motion as the only way to communicate a state.
understand.analogy: A user preference is like a setting on a device: the interface should adapt rather than insist on one presentation.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; transforms and animations follow the CSS rendering and timing model.

explain.narrative: The hover movement is removed when reduced motion is requested. The content and interaction remain available.

examples.explanation: The hover movement is removed when reduced motion is requested. The content and interaction remain available.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example demonstrating the relevant responsive or animation behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Add a non-essential animation to a card, then disable or simplify it under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Test both settings.
practise.independentTask: Build a small example that demonstrates the concept. Check keyboard access and reduced-motion behaviour where relevant.
hints: Test more than one viewport size.
Keep essential information available without motion.
Use developer tools to inspect computed values.

questions.prompt: Which media feature detects a request to reduce motion?
questions.explanation: prefers-reduced-motion reflects the user's reduced-motion preference.

questions.prompt: What should be done for users who prefer reduced motion?
questions.explanation: Respect the user's preference while preserving content and interaction.
